requirements.title: Party records are bitemporal and tenant-scoped
requirements.rationale: Parcels, consent and payments all attach to a person or organization. Without a party record there is nothing to attach them to. Bitemporality (ARCH-003) lets the platform answer what it believed about a party on the day a payment was authorized, not merely what is true now.

requirements.title: Identity evidence is referenced, never embedded
requirements.rationale: EVID-002 requires immutable cryptographically hashed originals. Identity documents live in evidence storage and are referenced by id and checksum, so personal documents are never copied into domain tables.

requirements.title: Party reads are confined to the owning tenant
requirements.rationale: This would be the platform's first operation reading an existing tenant-owned resource. SEC-006's cross-tenant check is presently unreachable from HTTP because every declared operation either creates a resource or is a stub.

requirements.title: Land roles distinguish farmer, landowner and land controller
requirements.rationale: The party working the land is frequently not the party who may commit it. Community and customary tenure often place authority with a controller who is neither the registered owner nor the farmer. Collapsing these three into one concept would either exclude customary tenure or misrepresent it as ownership.

requirements.title: Authority to commit land is established before conservation begins
requirements.rationale: Paying for conservation on land the counterparty had no authority to commit exposes the organization and the community to serious harm. A farmer role alone does not confer that authority; a landowner or land_controller role does.

requirements.title: Enrollment requires a recorded consent grant naming permitted uses
requirements.rationale: CONSENT-001 requires record-level permitted uses. Enrollment is the moment consent is obtained, so a party must not enter the platform without a grant naming what was agreed to, by whom, and in what language.

requirements.title: Consent withdrawal halts processing without destroying history
requirements.rationale: Consent that cannot be withdrawn is not consent. Withdrawal ends a grant's validity and blocks all future processing, while append-only history (ARCH-003) is preserved. OPEN QUESTION: this may not satisfy a legal right to erasure in every jurisdiction — see the proposal README.
